content.text:
I fixed one real spacing bug in `0.html` and otherwise left it alone, because the stylesheet is already in good shape. The change is not browser-tested: the command to locate Chrome for a render check was denied in this session, so it is verified only by reading the cascade. ## The bug In the common `

…

…` pattern, spacing broke in two ways: - **No gap below the title:** `header > :last-child` zeroed the heading's bottom margin, and only `body > header` had a margin of its own, so the title sat flush against the following paragraph. - **No gap above the section:** the rules that give 2rem of space above a section's leading heading only matched headings that were direct children, so one wrapped in a `

` got none. ## The fix - **`header` added to the block-flow margin rule** (`0.html:54`), so any header gets a 1rem bottom margin. `body > header` still overrides to 2rem. - **`header` added to the two sectioning selectors** (`0.html:42`, `0.html:48`), so a leading `
` gets the same 2rem top spacing as a bare heading, and the same collapse to 0 when it directly follows a heading. ## Left as is - **Tables:** `table { display: block }` can cost table semantics in some screen reader and browser combinations. The robust alternative is a wrapper element, which a classless stylesheet can't supply. - **Meta description:** there is no ``. The page is just a placeholder `0`, so I had nothing meaningful to write there.
